I think it’s a bummer that our lives coincided with the rise of addictive technologies that steal the one finite human resource: our time being conscious & alive. 

Young people thinking about their future should prioritize creating a life that avoids these technologies.

We don’t need this much information. We don’t need this much feedback. It serves nobody but the owners of the algorithms that amplify what they want you to see, read & hear — and shadowban what they want to suppress.

What I tweeted was intended to be the opposite - it was intended to remark on the difference between actual journalism that does the hard work of picking up the phone and accumulating new information (depicted in this scene) and the lazy work of producing media "content" (which is mostly just screaming into a webcam).  

The point was that we need more journalism and fewer hot takes and media "content." It's not a particularly profound point, but perhaps in haste I communicated it in a way that

So yesterday I tweeted this scene & made an offhanded comment that lots of media folk no longer understand media work as this particular kind of work anymore.

Some interpreted what I said as some sort of insult of journalists. So let me just respond.
